correctness.rationale: The rho_2 maximum is attained on a nonempty compact domain. The norm bound 3 and equality of BOTH distances imply ||x||=1, ||y_i||=2 and dual norm-one functionals simultaneously supporting x and z_i=-y_i/2; separation gives ||z_1-z_2||>=1. Conversely two star points with norm separation >=1 generate y_i=-2z_i and both distances exactly 3. Compactness of the supporting-functional incidence relation ensures the maximum diameter is attained, including nonsmooth vertices. In K_a the only non-singleton exposed faces are vertical segments of norm diameter 2sqrt(1-a^2); equality is a<=sqrt3/2. In P_N, vertex stars are pairs of incident edges; their endpoints have norm distance D_N=2sin(2pi/N) if 4|N and D_N=4sin(pi/N) otherwise. Edge distances are <=2tan(pi/N)<=D_N; checking trigonometric monotonicity gives N=4,6,8,10,12 exactly. The modulus statement follows from the single-face diameter threshold 1/2 at a=sqrt15/4. No exact subcritical rho_2 is proved.

originality.rationale: The originating full-text article defines the exact constant and the universal upper bound, with a sufficient bound via the modulus delta_K(1/2), but does not give a necessary-and-sufficient geometry-of-equality test or either sharp phase cutoff. The face-star criterion detects strict subcriticality in a specific interval where the published modulus bound cannot. This is a best-of-knowledge originality finding, not a claim to have ruled out all older norm equality criteria.
residual_risks: A classical but unindexed equality-in-triangle-inequality face-star lemma may phrase essentially the same rho_2 saturation criterion.
Only the threshold, not exact values of rho_2 below 3, is established; no claim that planar Rado numerical bound always improves.

A dimension-uniform iff saturation characterization and two exact sharp families determine when the universal bound is qualitatively improvable.
